mission: Prove development and agent readiness in hosted containers and on managed Linux workers: secure access, pinned toolchains, authorized authentication, isolated compute, and real beep-effect package proof.
statusNote: Opened 2026-10-01 at the operator's request after the first cloud probe session could not install dependencies (bun 1.3.14 vs pinned 1.4.2; bun.sh and pkg.pr.new denied by the environment's network policy). Accelerator: runs in parallel, takes no lane slot. Original cloud-session-setup.sh verification commands are historical; current bootstrap is scripts/cloud/bootstrap.sh. Lifecycle is unchanged. Expanded 2026-10-14 to managed Linux readiness under D8-D12 and L0-L4; stable packet id/path retained. Expanded 2026-10-23 through D40: protected tbk KVM worker qualified, host OS upgrades verified, dankserver bare-metal worker qualified for initial serialized development with all planned sign-ins complete and explicit Cursor/Meta quota holds, fleet skill published, and dedicated worker accounts corrected to the approved BEEP_SECRETS scope. The original cloud phases remain independently open. 2026-11-02 (D42): operator expanded cloud scope to Claude, Codex and Cursor setup on existing expiring credits only. P3 complete on #2486 (43d0a511). Claude environments saved on four accounts with two fresh smokes passing and two not yet collected (four-account qualification not claimed); Cursor bootstrap/snapshot built but no agent package proof; Codex bootstrap and package proof passed but reusable config publication fails, so Codex is not claimed runnable. P2, P4, P5, P6 and Linux L2/L4 remain open; lifecycle active. Receipt and blockers: history/2026-11-01-fleet-cloud-setup.md.

provenance.note: Authored directly from a cloud-session probe (research/2026-10-01-container-probe.md); no source exploration. The operator's expiring cloud credits (2026-10-08) are the payback-before-horizon test.

completionGate.statement: Not achieved until this goal's work ships as a PR driven to mergeable via /yeet (bun run beep yeet: repair -> verify -> publish --pr -> monitor). Per D4 the cloud session pushes and opens the PR through the GitHub API; the yeet monitor and closeout run operator-side.
